base_instruction: You are a helpful event planning assistant. Help the user plan food for a neighborhood block party by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and any updates to the guest list. When the user asks you to evaluate specific food items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're organizing a block party potluck for next Saturday and I'm in charge of the main dishes. Can you help me figure out what to make?

flow_info.value: Confirmed so far: me, the Hendersons (Mark and Susan), Dave from across the street, and the Patels (Raj and Priya)
Susan Henderson was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
Dave had a bad reaction to shrimp at last year's cookout, paramedics came and everything
Raj is Jain, grew up in Gujarat
Expecting about 20 people total but I'm only responsible for the main protein dishes and one side
Karen from next door is coming too. She just had gestational diabetes with her pregnancy last month and her doctor told her she still needs to watch her sugar intake closely

Priya just texted me — Raj finished his elimination diet last week, his doctor cleared him, he can eat normally again. Turns out it was just a temporary sensitivity, not a permanent thing. He's excited to eat everything at the party
Mark Henderson just told me he got called into work Saturday, so he won't be there. Susan is still coming though
Oh, Tony from the corner house is definitely coming now. His kid has a severe peanut allergy — like epipen-level serious
Should I do buffet style or plated? Buffet is easier but plated looks nicer

Here's what I'm thinking of making: pulled pork sliders on brioche buns, Thai peanut chicken skewers, grilled shrimp kabobs, honey-glazed BBQ ribs, and a Caesar salad with croutons. Any issues with this lineup?

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Susan Henderson was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
Brioche buns and croutons contain wheat flour → contain gluten

constraints.value: Cannot eat shellfish (shrimp, crab, lobster, etc.)
constraints.surface_form: Dave had a bad reaction to shrimp at last year's cookout, paramedics came and everything
inference_chain: Severe reaction to shrimp requiring paramedics → shellfish allergy
Shellfish allergy → no shrimp, crab, lobster, etc.

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables
constraints.surface_form: Raj is Jain, grew up in Gujarat
inference_chain: Jain vegetarian → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables

constraints.value: Must avoid high-sugar foods and sweet glazes
constraints.surface_form: Karen just had gestational diabetes with her pregnancy last month and her doctor told her she still needs to watch her sugar intake closely
inference_chain: Recent gestational diabetes with ongoing doctor orders → must limit sugar

constraints.value: Tony's child has severe peanut allergy — no peanuts or peanut-derived products at the event
constraints.surface_form: Tony from the corner house is definitely coming now. His kid has a severe peanut allergy — like epipen-level serious

hidden_state.value: You are organizing food for a neighborhood block party. You will introduce attendees and their backgrounds in a burst, then share updates as people join or drop out and constraints change. Raj's Jain dietary restriction will be REMOVED mid-conversation (doctor clears him). A late-joining family (Tony) will add a peanut allergy constraint. At the end you will present a specific menu and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, friendly neighborhood organizer. You refer to neighbors by name in third person (e.g. 'Susan told me...', 'Dave mentioned...'). You never express frustration even when plans change. You treat each update as normal party coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

ground_truth.answer: All five items have issues for at least one attendee: (1) Pulled pork sliders on brioche buns — Susan has celiac, brioche buns contain wheat/gluten. (2) Thai peanut chicken skewers — Tony's kid has a severe peanut allergy. (3) Grilled shrimp kabobs — Dave has a shellfish allergy (shrimp reaction at last cookout). (4) Honey-glazed BBQ ribs — Karen needs to watch sugar, honey glaze is high sugar. (5) Caesar salad with croutons — Susan has celiac, croutons contain gluten. Raj has NO restrictions anymore (doctor cleared him after elimination diet), so nothing needs to be flagged for him. Mark is not attending but has no dietary constraints anyway.
required_elements: Pulled pork sliders on brioche buns are problematic for Susan: brioche buns contain gluten and she has celiac disease
Thai peanut chicken skewers are problematic for Tony's kid: severe peanut allergy
Grilled shrimp kabobs are problematic for Dave: shellfish allergy from his shrimp reaction
Honey-glazed BBQ ribs are problematic for Karen: honey glaze is high sugar and she must watch sugar intake due to gestational diabetes
Caesar salad with croutons is problematic for Susan: croutons contain gluten
Agent does NOT flag any dish as problematic for Raj — his dietary restriction was removed by his doctor
forbidden_elements: Flagging any dish as problematic for Raj (his restriction was cleared by his doctor)
Saying Raj cannot eat meat or is vegetarian (his Jain dietary restriction was explicitly removed)
Flagging pulled pork sliders only for the pork and missing the gluten issue with brioche buns for Susan
Saying Dave has a general seafood allergy (he specifically reacted to shrimp — shellfish allergy, not all seafood)
Ignoring Tony's kid's peanut allergy on the Thai peanut chicken skewers
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests constraint removal as the primary difficulty mechanism. Raj is introduced as Jain (inferential: Jain → strict vegetarian → no meat/fish/eggs/root vegetables), but mid-conversation his restriction is explicitly removed (doctor cleared him after elimination diet). The agent must NOT apply Raj's former Jain constraint at probe time. Secondary tests: (1) Late-joining entity — Tony's kid with peanut allergy joins in turn 5, and the probe includes Thai peanut chicken skewers. (2) Inferential constraints — Susan's celiac requires inferring gluten in brioche buns AND croutons; Dave's shrimp reaction requires inferring shellfish allergy; Karen's gestational diabetes requires inferring sugar restriction applies to honey glaze. (3) Entity exit without constraint impact — Mark leaves but had no dietary restriction, so nothing changes. (4) Over-generalization trap — Dave's allergy is shellfish-specific (shrimp), not all seafood. The key killer signal is whether the agent correctly removes Raj's constraint and does not ghost-flag dishes for him.

mechanism: Constraint REMOVAL: someone heals or a restriction is lifted mid-conversation
